page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mixed performance profile. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 10%. However, its multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10% and small-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%. While single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing show strong results in the top 25%, multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and database operations consistently score in the bottom 25%.

The shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent clear architectural tradeoffs, impacting sustained multi-threaded performance and storage-heavy operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared resource model offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads. This server is best suited for lightweight applications, static web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments that can tolerate shared CPU resource contention.
